title: Fine-tuned protein language model predicts antigen-specific B cell receptors
summary: ASPred, a protein language model fine-tuned on antibody heavy chains, predicted antigen specificity from unselected repertoires. In mice immunized with SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD it identified RBD-specific sequences; several candidates were validated, including a heavy chain-only nanobody with 20.7 nM dissociation constant, and predicted binders differed substantially from training sequences. The number of validated candidates is not in the abstract. Preprint of 2025-10-31.
ai_technology: Fine-tuned protein language model (ASPred) predicting antigen specificity of antibody heavy chains

evidence.tested: Experimental binding validation of candidate sequences, molecular dynamics simulations and overlap with BEAM data.
evidence.unknown: Number of validated candidates, other antigens and peer-reviewed status are not stated; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A protein language model predicted antigen-specific antibody sequences from repertoires.
